title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the single source of truth for teams and managers to understand required approvals, owners, SLAs, and the templates to use for common operational flows.

Table of contents
1. Access & Permissions
2. Change Management
3. Data Management
4. Procurement & Expenses
5. Vendor Management
6. Travel Policy
7. Internal Templates and Forms
8. Governance, Exceptions, and Contacts
9. Revision history

1. Access & Permissions

Intro
Redwood grants system access on the principle of least privilege. Access decisions balance productivity with security and privacy requirements. This section describes request paths, role definitions, periodic review cadence, and emergency access procedures.

Role definitions (summary table)
- Role: Org Admin — Typical owner: Head of Engineering / IT Security — Typical permissions: full tenant-level settings, billing, user management.
- Role: Service Owner — Owner: individual engineering manager — Permissions: service configuration, deployment controls, runtime logs.
- Role: Read-Only Analyst — Owner: Data/Analytics manager — Permissions: dashboards and read-only telemetry.
- Role: Contractor — Owner: sponsoring manager — Permissions: scoped to project repos and dev environments; time-limited.

Access request procedure (numbered steps)
1) Initiate: Submit an Access Request form (Template: Access-Request-Form) with justification, requested role, and duration.
2) Approval: Manager approval required. For privileged roles (Org Admin, Production Deploy), approvals from People Ops and Security required.
3) Provisioning: IT/Identity team performs provisioning in the identity provider (Okta) and documents the change ticket ID.
4) Verification: Requestor confirms access within 48 hours.
5) Review: Quarterly access review; owners receive automated reports and must certify or revoke access.

Emergency access (break glass)
- Process: Request via PagerDuty escalation to on-call SRE + IT Security. A temporary elevated session (max 4 hours) can be issued after verbal approval from SRE lead and Security on-call. All sessions must be recorded and reviewed within 5 business days.

2. Change Management

Purpose
All changes that affect production systems, customer data, or network topology must follow the change management process to minimize outages and ensure traceability.

Change categories
- Standard change: Low-risk, pre-approved changes (routine infra patching, certificate renewals).
- Normal change: Requires change ticket, testing evidence, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency change: Immediate mitigation for incidents; requires post-facto review.

Change workflow (high level)
1) Submit RFC: Create a Change Request in the change management tool with scope, rollback plan, impact assessment, test plan, and owner.
2) Review & Approve: Normal changes require approval from the service owner and platform release manager. Changes impacting multiple services require SRE and security review.
3) Schedule: Book a maintenance window in the official calendar.
4) Execute: Follow runbook steps; ensure monitoring and rollback hooks are in place.
5) Post-change validation: Run smoke tests and update runbooks.
6) Retrospective: Document outcomes for any failed or emergency changes and create follow-up tasks.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Standard maintenance windows: Saturdays 02:00–02:00 UTC for non-customer-impacting infra work.
- Blackout periods: Major product launches and quarterly financial close weeks — no scheduled changes without executive approval.

3. Data Management

Scope and objectives
This section covers data classification, handling, retention, encryption, backups, and access controls for production and non-production data.

Data classification
- Public: Data safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: Company-internal data (default).
- Restricted: Customer data or information protected by contract or regulation.
- Confidential: Sensitive PII, secrets, or compliance-bound artifacts.

Handling and storage requirements (summary)
- Encryption: All Restricted and Confidential data must be encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Backups: Daily incremental backups for production datasets; full weekly backups with quarterly restore tests.
- Masking & use in non-prod: Production data used for testing must be sanitized or provided via a controlled snapshot process.
- Logging retention: Security logs retained for 365 days; application logs retained per service SLA (default 90 days).

Data retention and deletion
- Retention schedules are set per dataset and captured in the Data Inventory. Data owners must document retention justification and deletion process.
- Deletion requests (including customer data erasure) must be submitted via the Data Deletion request template and completed within SLA: 30 days for standard requests, 7 days for urgent customer erasure requests when contractually required.

Data access controls and auditing
- Principle: Role-based access via groups managed in the identity provider.
- Periodic audits: Data owners must certify access lists quarterly. Audit logs for data accesses to Restricted/Confidential datasets are retained for 365 days and reviewed monthly for anomalies.

4. Procurement & Expenses

Overview
Procurement is governed to ensure fiscal responsibility, vendor compliance, and proper expense tracking. This section outlines approval thresholds, preferred vendors, and expense reimbursement rules.

Approval thresholds (table)
- < $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Department head approval + Finance notification.
- > $25,000: Procurement committee + Finance director approval; may require PO and contract review.

Procurement steps (numbered)
1) Sourcing: Preferred vendors list should be consulted. For new vendors, complete the Vendor Intake form and route to Finance & Legal for risk review.
2) Quote collection: Get at least two competitive quotes for purchases > $5,000.
3) PO creation: Finance issues PO for approved requests.
4) Receipt and closeout: Confirm goods/services received, submit invoice to Finance with PO reference.

Expense reimbursement
- Submit expenses via the corporate expense system within 30 days.
- Required receipts: all items > $25. Exceptions must be documented and justified.
- Travel-related meal limits: US domestic — $75/day per diem; international per diem follows government guidance and must be pre-approved for high-cost regions.

5. Vendor Management

Objectives
Vendor management ensures vendors meet contractual SLAs, security expectations, and privacy commitments. It centralizes onboarding, security reviews, and periodic performance assessments.

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Completed Vendor Intake form.
- Security questionnaire completed (for vendors handling Restricted or Confidential data).
- Contract with clearly defined SLAs, data processing addenda (DPA) if applicable, and termination clauses.
- Finance setup completed and PO/contract filed.

Ongoing vendor oversight
- Quarterly business reviews for strategic vendors.
- Security re-assessments annually or on major product changes.
- Performance metrics: uptime, latency, incident response time, and change notice windows captured in a vendor scorecard.

Offboarding
- Revoke credentials and terminate network access.
- Confirm data return or secure deletion as specified in contract.

6. Travel Policy

Principles
Travel should balance employee safety, cost-effectiveness, and business need. Wherever possible, teams should prefer remote-first collaboration; travel must be pre-approved when in-person presence is required.

Booking and approvals
- Book via the corporate travel portal.
- Manager approval required for all travel. Travel over $2,000 total requires director-level approval.

Allowed expenses and limits
- Flights: Economy for flights < 6 hours; Premium Economy allowed for flights 6–9 hours with manager pre-approval.
- Hotels: Moderate business hotels on the corporate preferred list.
- Meals: See Procurement & Expenses section for per diems.

Safety and insurance
- Company travel insurance covers approved business travel. Employees must register international travel with People Ops for safety alerts and evacuation assistance.

7. Internal Templates and Forms

This section centralizes links and short descriptions for the canonical templates used across the company. Teams must use these templates to ensure traceability and consistent approvals.

Mandatory templates (examples)
- Access-Request-Form — for all system access requests.
- Change-Request-RFC — required for Normal/Emergency changes.
- Vendor-Intake-Form — for initiating vendor evaluations.
- Expense-Reimbursement-Form — for employee expense submissions.
- Data-Deletion-Request — for customer or data erasure requests.

Where to find templates
All templates are stored in the corporate templates library (Confluence page and the shared Google Drive / Templates folder). Templates include usage notes and example completions.

8. Governance, Exceptions, and Contacts

Exceptions
- Minor exceptions (e.g., temporary dev access) can be approved by the team manager and must be recorded in the Exceptions register with a time-limited approval (max 30 days).
- Major exceptions (security or compliance impact) require Security + People Ops approval and documented mitigations.

Escalation and contacts
- Security incidents: security@redwood.example / Security on-call via PagerDuty.
- Procurement questions: procurement@redwood.example / Finance helpdesk.
- Travel assistance: people-ops@redwood.example.
- Access & identity: identity-team@redwood.example.

Appendix: Quick checklists (copyable)

Access request quick checklist:
- Requestor name and email
- Justification and business impact
- Requested role and duration
- Manager approval attached
- Relevant training completed (if privilege requires)

Change request quick checklist:
- Owner and rollback owner
- Rollback plan and test steps
- Monitoring metrics to observe during change
- Stakeholders notified

Procurement quick checklist:
- Vendor intake completed
- Two quotes attached (> $5,000)
- PO or contract reference included

Contact and ownership
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (people-ops) — people-ops@redwood.example
- Security reviewer: Marco Ruiz — security@redwood.example
- Finance contact: Priya Singh — finance@redwood.example
